A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LOGICXGNN framework. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: V1 Section 4 reports original classification results on HIN, BBBP and Mutagenicity, alongside extracted chemical rules and generated graph examples.

after.justification: V2 reports original classification, runtime, robustness and graph-generation results in Section 4 and Appendices A.4–A.11.

M1.justification: The extraction, rule construction and grounding pipeline, including Algorithm 1, is retained. A limited generation extension appears in v2 Appendix A.11: a known molecule's descriptive clause is modified by adding or removing predicates before graph assembly. V1 describes clause sampling and reconstruction, leaving further clause manipulation to future work.

E1.justification: V2 retains Mutagenicity, BBBP and HIN, and adds BAMultiShapes, NCI1, IMDB-BINARY, PROTEINS, AIDS, BACE and SIDER, plus Cora/PubMed node classification. HIN classification moves to Appendix A.5, while its generation examples disappear. This substantially expands tested domains and tasks. MUTAG remains the papers' alternative name for the 4,337-graph Mutagenicity dataset.

E2.justification: GraphTrail becomes an evaluated classification and knowledge-extraction comparator in v2 Table 1, Figure 2 and Table 15. The HIN comparison replaces GLGExplainer with GraphTrail (v1 Table 1; v2 Table 9). GCNeuron moves from qualitative experimental comparisons to background/taxonomy discussion, while XGNN remains the molecular-generation baseline. These changes materially strengthen and revise the comparator set.

E3.justification: V2 adds runtime measurement, weighted precision/recall/F1, a four-architecture evaluation grid, Murcko scaffold-based 80:20 tests and fivefold rule-stability evaluation. The reported BBBP sample count changes from 2,039 to 2,050; the ordinary 80:20 split is retained. Newly disclosed optimizer and early-stopping settings do not establish changes to v1's previously unspecified training procedure.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's selected chemical and generation examples, v2 adds systematic architecture robustness, scaffold-distribution-shift and rule-stability analyses (Tables 11–13). Appendix A.10 adds clause-coverage histograms and representative-rule analyses, while A.11 expands generation case studies with multiple variants. These provide substantial new diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without run counts or uncertainty. V2 first specifies three random seeds and reports means and standard deviations for runtime, classification metrics and scaffold tests, alongside fivefold results. This introduces systematic variability reporting; it does not establish how many runs underlay v1.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive accuracy, runtime, classification-metric and robustness results. Reported BBBP rule-classifier accuracy changes from 81.37% to 83.58%, and Mutagenicity discriminative clause counts change from 198/167 to 184/158 (v1 Table 1; v2 Tables 1 and 15). These are revised reports, not established identical-setting gains. V1's training accuracies, predicate counts and descriptive-rule counts disappear, while chemical and generated-graph findings are expanded.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.4 adds an informal computational-complexity argument assigning O(|V|), O(|V||G|) and O(|V|) costs to the three stages. The central predicate definitions, DNF construction and grounding mathematics remain unchanged. No formal correctness theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and central extraction, knowledge-discovery and generation claims largely persist. V2's introduction adds explicit claims of superior accuracy against state-of-the-art global explainers and 10–100 times faster runtime, while associating outperformance of original GNNs with well-structured datasets. These refine and strengthen the existing contribution claims.

C2.justification: V2 develops a structural-regularity explanation for success on molecular graphs and explicitly discusses performance gaps on less regular graphs. It adds interpretations of rule coverage and stability, and substantial criticism of baseline filtering and concept limitations. Appendix A.11 acknowledges that systematic quantitative generation benchmarking remains future work. V1's regression-extension discussion is dropped; the general oversight caution largely carries over from its Impact Statement.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents Adam with learning rate 0.005, a 500-epoch maximum, 100-epoch warm-up, 50-epoch stopping patience, dataset statistics and baseline reproduction choices, including GLGExplainer filtering and threshold handling. Hardware changes from 32 GB RAM and a 2.7 GHz processor to 128 GB and AMD EPYC 7532. However, v1's hidden dimension of 32 and explicit handling of conflicting class rules are no longer specified.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantial positioning against GraphTrail, a functionality taxonomy, and detailed criticism of GLGExplainer's reliance on local explanations, domain knowledge and filtering (Sections 4–5; Appendices A.1 and A.3). It removes v1's explicit NEUROLOGIC lineage paragraph while retaining that citation, and adds references supporting oversmoothing, GIN/GAT, datasets and chemical interpretations.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the contribution list, evaluation narrative and conclusion. Section 3.4 changes from Extensions to Analysis, and experimental setup and generation discussion are reorganized within an appendix containing eleven subsections. The standalone Impact Statement is condensed into the conclusion. The abstract and most core methodological prose remain similar.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a single-column layout and redesigns Table 1 around accuracy and runtime, with rule-count comparisons appearing in Table 15. Figure 2 becomes a comparison across methods; Figure 3 changes generated examples and drops HIN. Numerous tables, histograms, rule panels and a generation gallery are added. The original generation walkthrough is retained as Figure 8, rather than being a new analysis.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's narrow evaluation through a stronger rule-based comparator, uncertainty reporting, broader task coverage, and architecture, distribution-shift and rule-stability tests. Added training details and explicit failure conditions improve assessability. Tradeoffs remain: some implementation disclosures disappear, and Table 1 supports only about 5–7 times faster runtime than GLGExplainer despite the broader 10–100 times claim. The gains in empirical support and understanding of applicability nevertheless constitute a substantial overall improvement.
